doubts.claim_under_doubt: a resync always either succeeds cleanly or fails loudly via CodexHooksSyncError
doubts.disproof_attempt: The stale-launcher cleanup loop (shared/scripts/tools/codex_hooks_sync.py:140-143) does a bare `existing.unlink()` with no exception handling, unlike every other write in this module's dependency chain (`durable_atomic_write`/`replace_retrying` explicitly retry past exactly this class of Windows PermissionError, per atomic_write.py's own module docstring on 'a concurrent READER can defeat the rename'). The iterate spec (`2026-09-22-r1b-codex-hooks-config-layer-shim.md:164-168`) explicitly designs this tool to be re-run 'at update-time' -- i.e. while OTHER, already-running Codex CLI sessions on the same machine may still be executing hooks loaded from the OLD `hooks.json` (the file is explicitly documented as global and trust-independent, shared by every Codex CLI invocation on the machine). If a resync changes the hook set (any bundle rebuild that adds/removes/reorders a hook shifts every `_launcher_slug(event, matcher, group_idx, handler_idx)` for events after the change, since the slug is derived from positional index, not identity), a launcher file that a concurrently-running session is mid-executing (or about to spawn via `cmd.exe /C "<launcher>"`) can be exactly the file this loop tries to unlink. On Windows, deleting an open-for-execution file without FILE_SHARE_DELETE raises PermissionError/OSError -- which is NOT caught here and is NOT among the exceptions `main()` catches (only `CodexHooksSyncError`, codex_hooks_sync.py:309-313). The result: an uncaught traceback out of what the module's own docstring calls a design that must 'surface loudly, never route around silently' -- inconsistent with every other error path in the file, which is wrapped. Note hooks.json + the sidecar are already durably published by this point (steps before the loop), so the important state isn't corrupted -- only cleanup is interrupted and the crash is ugly rather than the write being lost.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: wrap the unlink loop in a try/except that swallows FileNotFoundError and (on Windows) a transient sharing-violation PermissionError with the same retry-then-give-up discipline `atomic_write.py` already uses elsewhere in this codebase -- or at minimum catch OSError there and re-raise as CodexHooksSyncError so main() still prints the clean 'error: ...' message instead of a raw traceback. Alternatively, an explicit rebuttal that no realistic operator workflow re-runs this while another session's hook could be mid-fire against a slug the new run drops would resolve it -- but the spec's own 'update-time-run' framing argues against that.
doubts.resolution: FIXED: the stale-launcher unlink loop (codex_hooks_sync.py) now catches FileNotFoundError (pass) and OSError (logs a warning to stderr and continues) instead of propagating -- hooks.json and the sidecar are already durably published by this point, so a cleanup failure is now cosmetic (orphaned launcher, retried next sync) and never crashes the process. Regression test: test_stale_launcher_removal_survives_unlink_failure (monkeypatches Path.unlink to raise PermissionError for every launcher-dir file, asserts sync_codex_hooks still returns applied=True).

doubts.claim_under_doubt: an empty bundle_hooks result is a legitimate 'nothing to sync' state, not something that needs to be surfaced
doubts.disproof_attempt: `_materialize` guards ONE malformed-bundle shape explicitly (an empty `command` string raises CodexHooksSyncError, codex_hooks_sync.py:256-261, with the comment 'a malformed bundle, not an absence signal' -- directly echoing the module's own CodexHooksSyncError docstring principle at lines 62-65). But there is no equivalent guard for the coarser case: `_read_bundle_hooks` returning `{}` (or every event mapping to an empty group list) because `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`'s `hooks.hooks` was built from a corrupt/partial/interrupted `build_codex_plugin.py` run rather than because Shipwright genuinely has zero hooks. In that case `_materialize` returns `({}, [])`, `wanted_names` becomes the empty set, and the stale-cleanup loop (line 140-143) deletes EVERY existing launcher script, while `_strip_shipwright_entries` + the (now-empty) `new_hooks` merge silently removes every Shipwright entry from hooks.json -- globally disabling all Shipwright hook automation for every Codex CLI session on the machine, with no warning, no confirmation, and (per the spec's own Non-Goals, lines 181-186) no shipped un-sync/restore tool beyond hand-editing via the sidecar. This is exactly the 'absence signal' failure mode the module's own docstring says must never happen silently, just applied at bundle granularity instead of per-handler.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: raise CodexHooksSyncError when `bundle_hooks` (from _read_bundle_hooks) is empty or produces zero manifest_entries, unless an explicit `--allow-empty`/force flag is passed -- or a rebuttal showing build_codex_plugin.py structurally cannot produce a well-formed-but-empty hooks.hooks map (I did not verify that upstream invariant; it is outside this diff).
doubts.resolution: FIXED: sync_codex_hooks now raises CodexHooksSyncError when manifest_entries is empty unless the new allow_empty=True parameter (--allow-empty on the CLI) is passed. Regression test: test_empty_bundle_raises_unless_allow_empty.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: ownership-by-directory only ever claims (and deletes) files this tool itself wrote
doubts.disproof_attempt: `_is_shipwright_entry` (codex_hooks_sync.py:199-205) and the stale-cleanup loop treat directory membership under `codex_home/shipwright-hooks/` as sufficient proof of Shipwright ownership, with no marker/metadata check beyond location. Any file an operator (or a different tool) later places inside that directory -- by hand, by mistake, via a symlink, a backup copy, etc. -- is silently claimed: if its filename never matches a freshly-computed `wanted_names` slug, the very next sync deletes it with no log line identifying what was removed. This is a deliberate, previously-reviewed tradeoff (the module docstring explains why exact-triple matching was rejected instead), so the risk direction just moved rather than being new, but it's still an irreversible delete gated purely on path, worth a written acknowledgment.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: either accepted as-is (the directory name is unambiguous and the tool owns it exclusively by convention) or the unlink loop logs each removed filename so an operator has a trail to notice an unexpected deletion.
doubts.resolution: FIXED: the unlink loop now prints 'removed stale launcher: <path>' to stderr on every successful removal, giving an operator a trail.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: launcher scripts are created with an appropriately conservative permission set
doubts.disproof_attempt: On POSIX, a brand-new launcher is written via `durable_atomic_write` (base mode 0600 from `tempfile.mkstemp`, since `carry_destination_mode` has nothing to carry for a not-yet-existing destination), then `_write_launcher` (codex_hooks_sync.py:236-240) ORs in `S_IXUSR|S_IXGRP|S_IXOTH`, producing 0711 (rwx--x--x) rather than 0700 -- group and other gain EXECUTE (not read/write) on a Shipwright-authored hook launcher inside a directory (`shipwright-hooks/`, default `mkdir` mode ~0755) that other local accounts can traverse. Exploitability requires a genuinely shared multi-user machine with a permissive home-directory mode -- atypical for Shipwright's primary single-user-laptop target, and content stays unreadable/unmodifiable by others -- so this is informational, not blocking.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: chmod 0700 instead of OR-ing group/other execute bits, or an explicit note that this is accepted for the single-user target audience.
doubts.resolution: FIXED: chmod now ORs only S_IXUSR (owner-only execute), producing 0700. Regression test: test_posix_launcher_is_owner_only_executable.

summary: 4 doubts (1 high, 1 medium, 2 low), all fixed with regression tests. Verified as sound (not doubted further): the file_lock scope correctly covers the whole read-strip-materialize-write sequence including the launcher directory, so no torn window exists between hooks.json/sidecar/launchers under normal concurrent-sync contention (tested); crash-safety across the write-new-then-delete-stale ordering is genuinely self-healing (idempotent slug generation off deterministic bundle-build ordering) so a crash between any two of the three durable_atomic_write/unlink steps leaves the system in a consistent or self-repairing state on the next run, matching the code-reviewer's already-applied HIGH fix; the double-wrapped bundle-hooks shape and the sidecar-absence ownership regression are both explicitly tested against the real on-disk shape.
